text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert — canary error spike in EU-west. source=canary-healthcheck severity=page count=3p50m. Links: https://telemetry.redwood/eu-canary-traces/1769998765

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-90127 created for service: inference-canary-eu-west. Escalation policy: eng-oncall -> sre-lead.

ben (eng-oncall): Acked PD. I'm on it. Seeing 5xx rate jump from ~0.5% to 18% on the canary.

alice (runtime): Hey, any deploy in last 30m? deploy-bot: canary rollout 2026-11-02T03:12 initiated for model-serving:v2-quant.

ben (eng-oncall): Yep that matches. Rolling canary started 03:12 UTC. Traces show kernel OOMs + some segfaults on GPUs in eu-west-1b.

alice (runtime): I can tail the canary pods. Running: kubectl -n prod get pods -l release=canary-model-v2

ben (eng-oncall): Paste logs if you see anything obvious.

alice (runtime): Logs showing frequent: `RuntimeError: kernel_launch_failed: out of memory` then `Segmentation fault (core dumped)` on hosts gpu-eu-03 and gpu-eu-04.

alice (runtime): Snippet:

```
[2026-11-02T03:23:18Z] model-serving container[pid=4212]: kernel_launch_failed: cuCtxPushCurrent failed: CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_OUT_OF_RESOURCES
[2026-11-02T03:23:19Z] model-serving container[pid=4212]: Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

ben (eng-oncall): Hmm, v2-quant uses the new fused attention kernels that need a driver >= 530.x. Can someone check driver version on those hosts?

alice (runtime): ssh'd into gpu-eu-03: driver=525.85.05. So older than recommended. That could explain kernel failures. But why only canary? Maybe different kernel selection for quant profile.

carol (sre-lead): @ben @alice good catch. If driver mismatch causes kernel failures we should stop routing traffic to canary and roll it back to the previous model variant. Ben, can you divert traffic?

ben (eng-oncall): On it. Switching traffic for eu-west to baseline variant (model-serving:v1-stable) for live traffic. running: rdp route patch --service=inference --region=eu-west --variant=baseline

deploy-bot: Traffic shift initiated: 60% -> baseline, 40% -> canary.

ben (eng-oncall): Increasing to 100% baseline now.

deploy-bot: Traffic shift complete. Canary receives 0% production traffic.

alice (runtime): Canary pods still failing but at least production impact should be reduced. Telemetry shows p50 latency stable, 5xx down to 1.2% in eu-west within 90s.

eva (product): Any customer-facing impact? Are we seeing errors on logged-in customers or just internal healthchecks?

ben (eng-oncall): Public-facing: some external requests to a small subset of EU tenants (traffic routed to canary during rollout window) saw 5xx. Estimated affected sessions ~120 over 18 minutes. No billing issues reported. Will follow up with customer support for the small list.

carol (sre-lead): Next steps: 1) rollback canary image to v1-stable in deployment pipeline to prevent accidental re-release; 2) create a block in the rollout pipeline for v2-quant on eu-west until drivers are validated; 3) open a driver remediation ticket with infra to schedule node reimage to recommended driver or add capability detection in runtime.

alice (runtime): I opened infra ticket INFRA-3421 to update drivers on gpu-eu-* and added a preflight check to detect driver version before loading fused kernels.

ben (eng-oncall): I'm going to pin the canary image to not auto-retry and then start a controlled rollback. run: rdp deploy rollback --service=inference --to=model-serving:v1-stable --target=canary

deploy-bot: Rollback job queued. ETA ~2m.

ben (eng-oncall): Rollback complete. Canary pods replaced by v1-stable. Observability: no new segfaults, healthchecks green.

carol (sre-lead): Good. Assigning follow-ups: INFRA-3421 (driver upgrade), RUNTIME-1187 (preflight driver check), RELEASE-2105 (block v2-quant for eu regions until verified).

ben (eng-oncall): I'll run an org-wide postmortem tomorrow. For now, handing off to @dave (eng-oncall-next) for overnight watch. All escalation notifications taped to PD.

dave (eng-oncall-next): Taking handoff. Thanks team. I'll keep an eye on eu-west for 2 hours and will escalate if anything creeps up.

incident-bot: Incident PD-90127 acknowledged and status changed to Mitigated. Postmortem scheduled.

ben (eng-oncall): Quick note for customer success: affected tenants list exported to SRE drive -> https://drive.redwood/sre/incidents/PD-90127/affected-tenants.csv. Eva, recommend we coordinate a short email for impacted tenants offering context and status.

eva (product): Got it. I'll draft an incident message and sync with legal if wording needs to be conservative.

carol (sre-lead): Closing the active page. If any residual alerts escalate, re-open PD and tag me. Great quick coordination. :thumbsup:
